parts.label: a
parts.technique: Calculating Swt and Stt (regression/correlation summary statistics)
parts.reason: This is preparatory calculation for regression/correlation; S2.2 explicitly excludes 'calculations involving regression lines' and these sums (Swt, Stt) exist solely to compute regression coefficients and PMCC, which are excluded topics.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Sss, Sst summary statistics for regression
parts.reason: Same as (a); these values feed directly into the excluded regression line calculation (S2.2 exclusion) and PMCC (S5.1 exclusion).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Product moment correlation coefficient calculation via formula
parts.reason: S5.1 explicit exclusion: 'calculation of correlation coefficients is excluded' and 'use of the formula is not required'; here the formula is required.

parts.label: d
parts.reason: Depends entirely on the value of r computed in the excluded part (c); a part that only makes sense after an out-of-spec part is OUT.

parts.label: e
parts.reason: S2.2 explicit exclusion: 'calculations involving regression lines are excluded'.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Regression line equation (s on t) via coding
parts.reason: Same explicit S2.2 exclusion on regression line calculations; also depends on (e).

parts.label: g
parts.reason: Depends on the regression line found in the excluded part (f), so it is OUT.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: E(X) of a general discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion: 'calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables is excluded'.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Var(X) of a general discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion covers variance of discrete random variables directly.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Forming linear equation from E(Y)=3 to find p
parts.reason: Requires using E(Y), the mean of a discrete random variable, which S4.1 explicitly excludes; the whole method depends on this excluded concept.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Writing probability distribution of Y using p found in (c)
parts.reason: Depends directly on the value of p obtained in the out-of-spec part (c) (which used excluded E(Y)); a part only making sense after an out-of-spec part is OUT.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Calculating P(S=30) via P(X=6)×P(Y=5) using independent events
parts.reason: Although the technique of multiplying probabilities of independent events (S3.1) is itself in spec, this value only makes sense using P(Y=5)=p from the probability distribution of Y established in the out-of-spec parts (c) and (d); a part that only makes sense after an out-of-spec part is OUT.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Constructing probability distribution of S=XY (or Y^2)
parts.reason: Depends on the probability distribution of Y from the out-of-spec parts (c)/(d), so this part is OUT.

parts.label: g
parts.technique: E(S) of a general discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion of mean of discrete random variables applies directly to E(S).

parts.label: h
parts.technique: Comparing E(X^2) and E(S) to decide higher total score
parts.reason: Requires E(X^2) and E(S), both means of discrete random variables, explicitly excluded by S4.1.
